input.quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only renewal mechanic in the document. Renewal terms are 1 year (acceptable), but the Agreement gives Customer no non-renewal notice right; the only exit is termination "for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice", i.e. an effective 90-day window that exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling (and sits at the walk-away boundary). We therefore target the fallback and add a Customer right to decline renewal on sixty (60) days' written notice, without shortening Vendor's own 90-day convenience notice (that convenience right is a separate T4C point, not flagged here). No renewal price-uplift mechanic exists anywhere in the Agreement, so the price-cap element is not engaged.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
